title: Running a mobile detailing round
audience: Car detailers who travel to clients' homes or workplaces and need to plan a round of jobs, bring their own water and power, and manage wash water on each site.
referencesAtStart: No regulator page is cited in this lesson. Source: the mobile car wash business plan uploaded for this lesson, structure only.
learningOutcomes: Plan a round of mobile jobs with an order, time windows, travel buffers and access checks for each stop.
Confirm water and power at each site, and choose a wash-water method that keeps run-off out of stormwater drains.
Load, run and close a round in a fixed order, and record start, finish and any delay.

instruction.heading: Plan the round before the first job
instruction.body: A mobile round is planned from the booking list, not from memory. Group the bookings by suburb, then set the order so that the most time-critical job comes first and the shortest travel is between stops. For each job, set a time window, and add a buffer for parking, set-up, pack-down and the drive to the next stop. A round that looks possible on a map can fail when a client's gate is locked or a driveway is blocked, so confirm access for each stop before you leave. Write down the gate code, the parking, the location of the tap and the power point, and any pets. The mobile car wash business plan uploaded for this course describes a mobile operation with set operating hours and a stated service radius. Use that structure as a model: write the hours and the area in the round sheet, and do not accept jobs that take you outside the area without a decision recorded. A round sheet should show, for each stop, the order, the window, the address, the access notes, the water and power arrangement, the vehicle, the package and the estimated time on site.

instruction.heading: Water, wash water and power on site
instruction.body: Water and power are often the constraints on a mobile round. Before you travel, confirm that the client has a tap and a hose within reach, and that the flow is adequate for the work. Carry enough water for the stops that do not have a tap, and measure how much water a typical job uses in your own practice before you plan a tank size. Wash water must not run into a stormwater drain. Capture the run-off with a containment method, and take it away for disposal at an approved point, or discharge it where the local rules allow. Do not let it run onto neighbouring property. For power, read the rated power on the nameplate of each tool before you connect it. Plug tools into an outlet with residual current device protection, and check the lead for damage before use. Do not overload a generator by running more tools than its rating allows. Place a generator outdoors, away from doors and windows, so that its exhaust cannot enter a building. Never run a petrol generator inside a garage or enclosed space.

instruction.heading: Vehicle, kit and handover
instruction.body: Load the vehicle in a fixed order, so that the same item is always in the same place. Store chemicals upright, labelled, in a secure compartment, and keep the safety data sheet for each product in the vehicle. Lift heavy tanks and generators with a plan, and use a trolley where one is available. Wear gloves and eye protection when handling chemicals, and closed footwear on wet or sloping driveways. On arrival, stop and reassess if the site has a hazard you did not expect, such as a slippery surface, live traffic, exposed wiring or an unstable load. When the work is done, walk the client through the finish, note any limit, and complete the handover note. Pack down the kit, check that no item has been left on the client's property, and clear the run-off area. At the end of the round, log the start and finish times, the travel time, the water and power used and any delay, and restock the vehicle for the next round.

procedure: Print the round sheet with the order, the window, the address, the access notes and the water and power arrangement for each stop.
Check the tank level, the power lead, the generator fuel and the chemical stock the night before.
Load the vehicle in the fixed order, with chemicals stored upright and the safety data sheets on board.
At each stop, confirm the access, the water and the power before unloading.
Record the condition of the vehicle, carry out the work, and complete the handover note.
Manage the wash water at each stop so that no run-off enters a stormwater drain or a neighbour's property.
Log the start and finish times, the travel time, the water and power used and any delay.
Clean and restock the kit at the end of the round, and note any item that needs repair or replacement.

workedExamples.situation: A round of four jobs across three suburbs. Job 2 has no outside tap at the client's address. Job 3 has an outdoor power point, but the owner's pressure washer and polisher would both be running on the one generator, which is rated for less than the two together.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you change before the round starts?
workedExamples.reasoning: Confirm the tap at job 2 with the client before leaving. If there is no tap, either carry enough water for that job, measured from your own trial, or move the job to the end of the round and ask the client whether a tap can be arranged. Charge for any extra water in the quote if it is not included. For job 3, do not run the pressure washer and polisher together on the generator. Read both nameplate ratings, run one tool at a time, and check that the generator is placed outdoors away from openings. Record both decisions on the round sheet so the team can see why the order and the water plan were changed.

equipmentAndPpe: Round sheet, printed or on a tablet, with access notes for each stop.
Water tank with a level gauge, sized from your own measured job use.
Residual current device protected lead and a generator rated for the tools it will run, where a generator is used.
Containment method for wash water, such as a catch sheet or a portable containment tray.
Spill kit and a suitable fire extinguisher in the vehicle.
Gloves and eye protection for chemical handling, closed footwear, and high-visibility clothing when working near traffic.

commonErrors.error: Booking back-to-back jobs with no buffer for travel, parking and set-up.
commonErrors.prevention: Add a buffer to each stop, based on a timed trial, and confirm the next stop's access before leaving.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a client has a tap or a power point without asking.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the water and the power for each stop in writing when the booking is made, and again before travel.

commonErrors.error: Letting wash water run into a stormwater drain.
commonErrors.prevention: Contain the run-off and take it to an approved disposal point, following the local rules for the site.

commonErrors.error: Overloading an outlet or a generator by running several large tools at once.
commonErrors.prevention: Read each tool's rated power, add them up, and run only what the outlet or generator can carry.

commonErrors.error: Carrying chemicals loose in the cabin or the boot.
commonErrors.prevention: Store chemicals upright, labelled and secured, and keep the safety data sheets in the vehicle.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wash water disposal and stormwater rules differ between councils, states and territories. Check them with the local council before you work in a new area.

Electrical equipment should be connected through residual current device protection and checked for damage before use. This lesson does not cover work on fixed or client wiring, and you must not alter or repair client wiring.
A generator must not be run in an enclosed space, and its exhaust must be kept away from doors and windows. The manufacturer's instructions for the generator govern its use.
Do not park in a way that blocks traffic or a driveway.

qualityStandard: A round sheet exists for every round, with order, window, access, water and power for each stop.
Water and power are confirmed for each stop before the work begins.
No wash water enters a stormwater drain or a neighbour's property during the round.
Start, finish, travel time, water and power use and any delay are logged for every round.
documentationEvidence: Round sheet with the order, windows, access notes and water and power arrangements.
Log of start and finish times, travel time, water and power used, and any delay.
Incident or near-miss note for any hazard, spill or equipment fault during the round.
summary: Plan the round from the booking list, with buffers and access checks for each stop.
Confirm water and power before the work, and keep wash water out of stormwater drains.
Load, run and close the round in a fixed order, and log every round.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before leaving for a round, what must you confirm at each stop?
options: Only the client's name and address
The client's favourite music in the car
Access, water and power at that stop

knowledgeChecks.question: Wash water from a driveway is about to run toward a stormwater drain. What is the right action?
options: Let it run, because it is only water and it will evaporate quickly in the sun
Capture it or direct it to an approved disposal point, and check the local rules
Add more soap so it drains faster, since the soap breaks down quickly outdoors

knowledgeChecks.question: A generator will run an electric polisher and a pressure washer. What must you avoid?
options: Overloading it with more tools than its rating allows
Running it outdoors, away from doors and windows
Checking its fuel before the round

Conditions vary by council, state and territory. The manufacturer's instructions, the site owner's rules and the local authority govern, and this lesson does not replace them.
